correctness.rationale: The Hadamard entry factorization H_{k tau+u,v tau+w}=N^{-1/2}chi_v(k)chi_w(u) and orthogonality over all u yield the exact Gram identity. The singleton-residue iff classification is constructive in both directions (repeat a block for necessity). Rank is bounded by sums of q rank-one factors per low residue. A nonzero high-frequency Walsh character on uniformly drawn blocks is an iid fair sign, so the two-plane Gram defect and rank-loss probability are exact. Exhaustive standard-library integer replay independently checked 169168 Gram comparisons and 25 support-count cases; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A generic OSE concentration statement or a cyclic Fourier erasure extremum does not establish the exact per-sample Gram identity, its classification of every coordinate support, or the independent-binomial spectrum. Both Fourier constructions share character orthogonality but their groups, partition structures, and sampling quantifiers are different.

evidence: The nearest two-character harmonic-frame result concerns cyclic Fourier erasures with an arithmetic gcd-controlled extremum; the full theorem does not cover Boolean dyadic blocks sampled with replacement.
Other related Walsh-frame spectra sample binary symplectic groups or Hamming balls, not an iid choice of contiguous Sylvester-Hadamard row blocks.
No exact dyadic-residue block-spectrum table was identified in the inspected sources.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Exact spectra on different finite group sampling sets are not an exact database or table for the sampling operator defined here. Negative retrieval cannot alone prove originality; the positive scientific non-implication of the closest inspected sources supports the comparison.

originality.rationale: Primary and related full-text scientific comparisons identify probabilistic OSE sufficient bounds, unlike the complete exact pathwise coordinate-support decomposition and binomial sampling law. The close cyclic Fourier erasure theorem was read in full and concerns a different group and deterministic extremization. Related Walsh spectra concern other restriction subsets. No dominating statement has been identified, subject to the disclosed folklore/equivalence risk.
residual_risks: Finite abelian Fourier character orthogonality is classical; an unindexed equivalent general Fourier-aliased block-sampling formulation could cover this exact specialization.
Full-text review is targeted to theorem-relevant material for the 29-page expanded preprint; sections unrelated to embeddings have not been exhaustively scanned.
Other published harmonic-frame results on different groups could admit an unrecognized reduction, though the inspected closest cyclic theorem does not.

value.rationale: The proof gives a complete natural classification and exact counts of all coordinate subspaces that are isometric under every sampled-block sequence, and exact binomial rank-failure on every remaining two-plane class. Identical block Frobenius leverage scores in both classes show that scalar score flatness does not resolve pathwise spectral stability. The number of independent blocks, not merely total rows, controls the rank-loss law. This is a motivated structural boundary for block-coded least-squares embeddings, beyond a toy numerical counterexample.
